title: Read the Order Logs
description:
**SITUATION:**

You're taking over the order-processor pager mid-shift. The outgoing engineer wants proof that you can find your way around its logs. They also left a **shift handoff code** that's announced in the live log every 30 seconds.

- `/var/log/order-processor/orders-2026-09-30.log`: yesterday's full log (thousands of lines)
- `/var/log/order-processor/live.log`: being written right now

**YOUR TASK:**

Every answer goes in `~/answers/` (create it first).

1. Browse yesterday's log with `less` (search, jump to the end, quit).
2. Count its lines. Save just the number to `~/answers/line-count`.
3. Save exactly its first 10 lines to `~/answers/first-10.txt` and exactly its last 5 lines to `~/answers/last-5.txt`.
4. Save exactly line 1500 to `~/answers/line-1500`.
5. Follow `live.log` as it grows and save the **latest** handoff code (6 characters) to `~/answers/handoff-code`. It rotates every 30 seconds, so submit soon after you write it.

**GOOD PRACTICES:**

- `less` doesn't load the whole file at once, so it's safe on huge logs. `cat` is not.
- Use `>` to save output instead of copying text from the terminal.
- `tail -f` keeps following the file until you press `Ctrl+C`.

hints: You are learner on a real Ubuntu machine with systemd; sudo works without a password.
Reset gives you a fresh machine (your changes are wiped).
Read SPEC carefully, then Submit — the grader checks the machine itself.
problemStatement.solution:
# Solution — Read the Order Logs

Logs are the first thing you read in any incident. `less` is for browsing, `head` and `tail` grab the ends, `wc` counts, and `tail -f` follows a file as it grows.

Docs: `man less` · `man head` · `man tail` · `man wc`

## Browse

```bash
cd /var/log/order-processor
ls -lh
less orders-2026-09-30.log
```

Inside `less`: `Space`/`b` page down/up, `G` end, `g` start, `/ERROR` search, `n` next match, `q` quit.

## Answers

`>` sends a command's output into a file:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/answers
wc -l < orders-2026-09-30.log            > ~/answers/line-count   # < avoids printing the filename
head -n 10 orders-2026-09-30.log         > ~/answers/first-10.txt
tail -n 5  orders-2026-09-30.log         > ~/answers/last-5.txt
sed -n 1500p orders-2026-09-30.log       > ~/answers/line-1500
# same thing with head/tail: head -n 1500 orders-2026-09-30.log | tail -n 1
```

## Follow the live log

```bash
tail -f live.log          # Ctrl+C to stop
```

A `NOTICE shift handoff code=...` line appears every 30 seconds. Write the newest code down quickly:

```bash
echo 'K3X9QA' > ~/answers/handoff-code
```

Then **Submit** before it rotates twice.
